groups.label: Start here
groups.description: New to digital forensics? These are the first doors to open.

items.label: Order of volatility (RFC 3227)
items.description: The rules for what to capture first — live memory before disk, disk before logs. Every investigation starts here.

items.label: NIST SP 800-86 — Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques
items.description: The canonical process for collecting, examining, analysing and reporting digital evidence.

items.label: DFIR Cheat Sheets (SANS)
items.description: Free reference posters for Windows artefacts, memory, and incident response.

items.label: 13Cubed — Digital Forensics
items.description: Accessible video walkthroughs of real forensic workflows, artefacts and tooling.

groups.label: References & community
groups.description: Hand-picked free resources for learning and practising digital forensics.

items.label: NIST Computer Forensics Tool Testing (CFTT)
items.description: Reference datasets and methodology from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology.

items.label: SANS Digital Forensics & Incident Response
items.description: Blogs, whitepapers, and training resources from the SANS Institute.

items.label: The DFIR Report
items.description: Real-world intrusion write-ups with timelines, tooling and defender takeaways.

items.label: Forensic Focus
items.description: Interviews, news and discussion from the wider digital forensics community.

items.label: DFIR Review
items.description: A curated directory of digital forensics tools, techniques, and references.

items.label: Forensics Wiki
items.description: Community-maintained wiki covering forensic techniques, tools, and methodologies.

items.label: MITRE ATT&CK
items.description: Knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques — essential for threat-informed analysis.

groups.label: Practice datasets
groups.description: Public, legal evidence for hands-on labs — disk images, memory dumps and packet captures.

items.label: NIST CFReDS — Computer Forensic Reference Data Sets
items.description: Reference disk, memory and mobile images with published hash values. This is the source for our Case File 001.

items.label: Digital Corpora — Digital Forensics
items.description: Public disk images and memory dumps curated for forensics training.

items.label: UNB CIC datasets
items.description: Publicly available network traffic captures for intrusion-detection practice and protocol analysis labs.

items.label: Malware-Traffic-Analysis.net
items.description: Real packet captures of malware infections, with exercises — ideal for network forensics practice.

items.label: VirusShare — curated malware samples
items.description: Malware corpora available to registered researchers — handle only inside isolated, authorised lab environments.

groups.label: DFIR tools
groups.description: The toolkit every analyst should know, grouped roughly by discipline.

items.label: Autopsy
items.description: Open-source digital forensics platform for disk imaging, timeline analysis and artefact extraction.

items.label: FTK Imager
items.description: Forensic imaging tool from Exterro for creating and verifying disk and memory images.

items.label: Eric Zimmerman's Tools
items.description: The de-facto standard suite of Windows artefact parsers — MFTECmd, PECmd, JLECmd, Registry Explorer and more.

items.label: KAPE
items.description: Kroll Artifact Parser and Extractor — targeted collection and processing of Windows artefacts.

items.label: Velociraptor
items.description: Endpoint visibility and digital forensics at scale, using VQL queries across many hosts.

items.label: Volatility 3
items.description: Memory forensics framework for analysing RAM dumps, processes and artefacts.

items.label: MemProcFS
items.description: Present a memory dump as a virtual file system for fast, scriptable memory analysis.

items.label: Wireshark
items.description: The standard open-source packet analyser for network forensics and protocol investigation.

items.label: YARA
items.description: Pattern-matching tool for identifying and classifying malware samples in forensic datasets.

items.label: CyberChef
items.description: The cyber swiss-army knife — decode, decrypt, parse and transform data in the browser.

items.label: Plaso (log2timeline)
items.description: Super timeline generation across filesystems, logs and artefacts into a single chronology.

items.label: Timesketch
items.description: Collaborative timeline analysis and annotation for investigations.

items.label: ALEAPP
items.description: Android Logs Events And Protobuf Parser for mobile app artefact extraction.

items.label: MobSF
items.description: Mobile Security Framework — static and dynamic analysis of Android and iOS apps.

items.label: REMnux / Flare VM
items.description: Purpose-built Linux and Windows distributions for malware analysis and reverse engineering.

items.label: ExifTool
items.description: Read, write and edit metadata across virtually every file format — a metadata workhorse.

groups.label: Standards & frameworks
groups.description: The rules of engagement that keep evidence admissible and the work defensible.

items.label: RFC 3227 — Guidelines for Evidence Collection and Archiving
items.description: Order of volatility: collect the most perishable evidence first.

items.label: NIST SP 800-86
items.description: Guide to integrating forensic techniques into incident response.

items.label: ISO/IEC 27037
items.description: International guidelines for identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence.

items.label: ISO/IEC 27041 / 27042
items.description: Assurance and analysis/interpretation of digital evidence.

items.label: SWGDE — Scientific Working Group on Digital Evidence
items.description: Practical, free guidance documents across forensic disciplines.

items.label: ACPO Good Practice Guide for Digital Evidence
items.description: The four ACPO principles for handling digital evidence, widely referenced in practice.

items.label: NIST SP 800-101 — Mobile Device Forensics
items.description: Guidelines on mobile device forensics, acquisition methods and preservation.

groups.label: Recommended reading
groups.description: The books and long-form references our members learn from.

items.label: File System Forensic Analysis — Brian Carrier
items.description: The deep reference on FAT, NTFS, HFS+ and how filesystems leak evidence.

items.label: The Art of Memory Forensics
items.description: Windows, Linux and Mac memory analysis — the memory forensics bible.

items.label: Practical Malware Analysis
items.description: A hands-on guide to dissecting malicious software safely.

items.label: Windows Forensic Analysis Toolkit — Harlan Carvey
items.description: The practical field guide to Windows artefact analysis.

items.label: Incident Response & Computer Forensics
items.description: The end-to-end incident response lifecycle, from triage to reporting.

items.label: Digital Forensics and Incident Response — Gerard Johansen
items.description: A practical introduction to incident response. Relevant to the T1486 ransomware scenario in Case File 002.

items.label: NIST SP 800-61 — Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
items.description: The canonical incident response lifecycle. Essential reading for Case File 002's ransomware scenario.

items.label: Plaso documentation
items.description: How to build super timelines from disparate artefacts — critical for Case File 003.

groups.label: Case investigation toolkit
groups.description: Tools referenced directly by our published case files.

items.label: Autopsy — Case File 001 primary analysis
items.description: Full disk image analysis, artifact extraction and keyword search.

items.label: Bulk Extractor
items.description: Scan raw disk images for PII, documents, and other salient features without parsing the filesystem.

items.label: RegRipper
items.description: Parse Windows Registry hives for user activity, USB history and evidence of execution.

items.label: libewf / ewfacquire
items.description: Handle E01/Ex01 forensic image formats described in case briefs.

items.label: Zeek
items.description: Network security monitor that converts PCAP into structured logs for analysis.

items.label: Ransomware decryption tools
items.description: Free decryption tools by ransomware family — relevant to the T1486 scenario in Case File 002.
